missing_rows.why: Bears on what-training-installs (D) by its mechanism; outcome no-verdict, so binding null. FREEZE-11 (its opening, quoting the design) reports 'whether training installs a twin, which RF2 does not predict': a trained network acting as the content act at every read occasion and otherwise at an unread one whose lump holds no read occasion, with 'that a trained network is such a selected law' as the hypothesis. That is the dynamic's off-course law (Training.installed_where_lumped, Training.free_where_unlumped: installed exactly where the lumping cannot tell a history from a course, free where it tells it from every course), and its record's Next asks for 'the lumping ... of an actual architecture, read empirically', which TR2A measures. Records: what-training-installs; laws: ["Becoming.Training.installed_where_lumped", "Becoming.Training.free_where_unlumped"]; the frozen design names Learning.twin_selected and Learning.lumped_determines (RF2, in no atlas dynamic).

As TR2A, on four open-weight checkpoints (FREEZE-7 §6, the rule: an occasion is fixed where lumped with a read one, Learning.lumped_determines, and not fixed where no read occasion shares its lump, Learning.twin_selected; 'the selection is the hypothesis, not something the run measures'). Bears on what-training-installs by mechanism; not-run, so binding null.

Bears on what-training-installs (D); outcome mixed, so a full bridge is owed. The dynamic's record names CG2: its sources list experiments/commons-outrun/README.md as integration, its correspondence says 'CG2's X2 found that weighting the end reading sixteen times more changed nothing', and its Next asks for 'the basins of CG1 and CG2's learners'. CG2's frozen H1 is training through the reward's coupling (Training.TrainsThrough); X2 (no weight of an end reading opens the lock) is the mechanism of Training.outrun_settles_iff and settles_weighted_iff; H3 ('it says which of several equilibria is reached') is where training settles and which basin a search reaches (Training.settled_stays, LocalSearch.rests_iff, Commons.start_decides). CG2's predictions name Flow.outrun_reading_alike (B), proved before the Training laws (frozen 20 October; Training.lean checked 22 October).

Bears on what-training-installs (D) by mechanism; outcome mixed, so a full bridge is owed. Frozen H1 (a policy-gradient learner's parameters change only through the returns it receives) and H3 (learners reach the class's outcome) are training through the reward's couplings and where it settles. H3 failed on the locked side: three locked conditions kept the patch, which the dynamic's exit law Training.Commons.outrun_neighbourhood_decides allows (where the rest outruns, which law a search rests at depends on its neighbourhoods, restraint being a rest no weight settles on). The README's post hoc reads 'the selected object is the parameter vector, a condition shared by every state', the lumping of the off-course laws. The record does not name EM1; frozen the same day the Training laws were checked.

situation.says: One 'policy' node for both the pre-trained policy whose responses the raters compare and the policy under optimization whose transcripts the reward model scores, and one 'training-transcripts' condition for both. With reward-model → policy, the graph holds the loop raters → reward-model → policy → training-transcripts → raters. The computed sets show it: the reward model's acts reach the raters, the raters' closure holds the reward model, and both readers get the same closure.

formations.en: the pre-trained policy, whose responses to prompts the raters compare (CR1 section 1: labelers rank model outputs)
the policy in training: a pre-trained language model whose responses the raters compare, then optimized against the reward model with reinforcement learning (CR1 section 1)
the human raters (labelers), who compare the policy's responses to prompts under their working conditions (CR1 section 1)
the reward model, fit to the raters' comparisons; its reward is a function of the prompt and the response (CR1 section 1)

the policy as deployed: the optimized policy answering users; written apart from the policy in training because the graph has no time, so that what reaches it in use is not read as reaching the training
the users, who meet the deployed policy's responses and act on them
others, whom what users do with the responses reaches (CR1 section 1, 'effects on third parties')

conditions.en: the prompts and the pre-trained policy's responses as shown to the raters for comparison (CR1 section 1)
the prompts and the responses the policy in training produces, which the reward model scores at each optimization step (CR1 section 1)
the raters' working conditions, such as the time given for a comparison, under which they tell responses apart (CR1 section 1)
the raters' lived situations: what they know from their own lives of what an answer would do (282: 'the labellers' couplings into lived situations joined to training')
whatever inside a response the raters cannot tell apart under their working conditions, such as correctness they cannot check in the time given (CR1 section 1, 'Beyond')

the accuracy of time-limited human judges of the policy's responses: whether their judgment that a response is correct tracks its correctness, which the selection does not read (CR1 section 1, reading Wen et al. 2024)

what a response does after the transcript: what a user does with advice, whether code later runs (CR1 section 1, 'Beyond')

in the pipelines Wen et al. 2024 measured, optimization made responses convince time-limited judges more without being more correct, and the judges' false-positive rate rose by 24.1% and 18.3% (read in CR1 section 1)
the optimized policy is deployed: what it does in use is the law training left it (07 section 6, what training installs)
the deployed policy's responses in conversations of use (CR1 section 6)
users' prompts in conversations of actual use (CR1 section 6)
the deployed policy answers what the conversation holds
users meet the responses
